newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Pulp market seen improving in 97 - Soporcel.
newsitem.headline: Pulp market seen improving in 97 - Soporcel.

text.p: The pulp market is expected to improve in 1997, compared with this year, but it is hard to estimate by how much, said Alvaro Barreto, president of Portugal's Soporcel-Sociedade Portuguesa de Papel.
"We think 1997 will be better than 1996," Barreto told Reuters.
"For 1997 we see the possibility that the market will improve, but there is no clear data," he added.
Soporcel expects to end 1996 with a cash-flow of at least 11.6 billion escudos, compared with 25.8 billion in 1995, Barreto said.
"We expect to close 1996 with a cash-flow that will be at least twice the 5.8 billion escudos posted in the first half," he said.
He declined to give further forecasts.
"I can only say that the second half (1996) will be moderately better than the first half," he said.
Soporcel posted a loss of one billion escudos and sales of around 30.4 billion escudos in the first six months.
The company posted a net profit of 11.2 billion escudos, a cash-flow of 25.8 billion escudos and sales of 76 billion escudos in 1995.
